task.description: Independently validate CODE-DESIGNER's design for the ISS-0515 tenant_template build-race fix before it proceeds to ELIXIR-DEV.

result.note: All 8 checks verified independently, trusting nothing in the handoffs' own claims. (1) No literal code: grep for defmodule/def /schema " ... do over the design doc returns zero matches -- prose and citations only. (2) THE load-bearing claim verified against actual ExUnit source at /home/tvolodi/.asdf/installs/elixir/1.20.3-otp-29/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit.ex lines 279-304: ExUnit.start/1 calls Application.ensure_all_started + configure/1, then registers a System.at_exit/1 callback and returns :ok immediately -- it never dispatches a test inline. System.at_exit callbacks only fire once the whole script-loading invocation (test_helper.exs plus all required test files) is about to terminate, so a synchronous blocking call anywhere in test_helper.exs (before or after ExUnit.start/1) is guaranteed to finish before any test process exists. Design's claim is correct. (3) Read test/test_helper.exs directly: current file has ExUnit.start(exclude: [...]) at line 52 followed immediately by ExUnit.after_suite(...) at line 54 -- the design's proposed insertion point (after start, before after_suite) is exactly where the file's existing structure would take a new one-time synchronous statement, consistent with the file's own established pattern (the two sweep_* calls already there). (4) Read tenant_template.ex lines 60-138: template_ready?/0 (line 137) reads a persistent_term marker set at line 126, checked at the fast-path guard on line 84 (if template_ready?() do :ok). This fast path is confirmed real and is exactly what the design relies on -- after pre-build, every real test's ensure_template!/0 call returns :ok without touching the lock-acquisition line 97. (5) grep confirms: no test drops the literal tenant_template schema (all DROP SCHEMA hits in test/ target staging/reference/randomized schema names, never the literal name); tenant_template_test.exs line 38 is use Letflow.DataCase, async: false. Both claims correct. (6) Design's own scope section (line 11) states no change to Letflow.TenantProvisioning or anything under lib/letflow/; confirmed by git diff --stat against base_commit 468079c4, which shows only the new design doc file touched, nothing under lib/. (7) Rejection of the timeout-bump alternative (design section 3) is grounded directly in the diagnosis's own unresolved section 4c/4d Sandbox.mode/2 anomaly plus a sound recurrence argument (a bigger timeout only widens the same race window as the fixture-needing test count grows) -- not an arbitrary preference, and consistent with the diagnosis's own recommendation to evaluate this risk before choosing option (b). (8) Design section 8 gives ELIXIR-DEV four concrete, actionable re-verification steps: a post-fix re-run of the diagnosis's own 5-way concurrency repro expecting fast-path :ok for all callers, two consecutive clean scripts/test_parallel.sh / mix letflow.check.test runs on the previously-failing commit, a timing sanity check against the ~1.8-1.9s baseline with the actual number to be reported, and a tenant_template_test.exs regression run -- these would genuinely demonstrate the race is eliminated, not merely given more headroom. No defects found. Design is unambiguous, fully scoped, and ready for ELIXIR-DEV.
